faults.page says: The governance page says IMMA is a Public Body and a Company Limited by Guarantee; the memorandum page says it is a Company Limited by Guarantee with charitable status. No cited page calls it a foundation.

faults.stored: ...the public foundation form is chosen because the state controls the board of this company.
faults.page says: The pages state company limited by guarantee, public body and ministerial appointment of directors; the foundation form is the researcher's inference.
faults.fix: IMMA's governance page says it is a Public Body and a Company Limited by Guarantee whose Board directors the Minister for Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport & Media appoints, and its memorandum page says it has charitable status approved by the Charities Regulator; a charitable company limited by guarantee is a private nonprofit.

faults.page says: The ad calls the company a public benefit company (hevra letoelet hatsibur) and a municipal corporation wholly owned by Haifa Municipality. It never says foundation.

faults.stored: The company's own job advertisement ... calls Haifa Museums a public benefit company and municipal corporation ...
faults.page says: The ad is hosted on the Israel Museums Association (ICOM Israel) site, not on the company's own site.
faults.fix: The Haifa Museums company's job advertisement, section Job description, as posted on the Israel Museums Association (ICOM Israel) site, calls the company a public benefit company and a municipal corporation wholly owned by Haifa Municipality that runs the city's museums, including the Haifa Museum of Art; a municipal corporation owned by the city is a municipal or regional body.
